A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C3 benchmark and contain readable main text, references, and Appendices A.1–A.4. All 19 pages, nine tables, and thirteen figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus analyses in Section 3.1, SDM benchmark results in Tables 2–3, and human–LLM agreement statistics and detailed results in Appendices A.3–A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original corpus analyses, SDM evaluations, human–LLM agreement statistics, and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and evaluation procedures in Sections 3.2–4 are unchanged, including LLM-based judging, manual audio assessment, and majority voting. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both retain English and Chinese coverage of phonological ambiguity, semantic ambiguity, omission, coreference, and multi-turn interaction. The source datasets and represented scenarios in Section 3 and Appendix A.1 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 and 6–9 retain the same ten evaluated SDMs, including GPT-4o-Audio-Preview, Qwen2.5-Omni, and Moshi. Their participation and exclusions by language and task are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,079 instances and 1,586 audio-text pairs, identical category counts, prompts, dialogue-history handling, model restrictions, accuracy metrics, and averaging of the two LLM judges.

E4.justification: Section 5.2.2 retains the same detection-versus-completion/resolution analysis, and Section 4.2 retains the same judge-reliability analysis. No ablation, robustness test, or additional case study is introduced or removed.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.3 retain the same Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlation reporting and corresponding p-values. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: The corpus statistics, Tables 2–9, and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4o-Audio-Preview's 55.68% English overall accuracy and Qwen2.5-Omni's 40.08% Chinese overall accuracy; Appendix A.4 retains the same judge-specific scores.

T1.justification: Neither version contains a formal theoretical contribution or proofs. The benchmark's definitions and category distinctions are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a bilingual benchmark covering five conversational phenomena and an LLM-based evaluation method aligned with human judgments. No core claim changes scope or strength.

C2.justification: The explanations of omission difficulty, language-dependent performance, and model-specific strengths remain unchanged. The Limitations section retains the same qualifications concerning other languages and human-evaluator bias.

D1.justification: The disclosed dataset, website, and code links are unchanged. Sections 3.2–4 and Appendices A.1–A.2 retain the same speech-generation, manual-checking, annotation, preprocessing, and prompt details.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the discussion of ADU-Bench and other spoken-dialogue benchmarks.

P1.justification: The displayed arXiv identification changes from v1 dated 30 July 2025 to v2 dated 25 September 2025. The prose, terminology, section structure, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes the printed page-number footers and has slight typesetting variations. All thirteen figures and nine tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, interpretations, and limitations, including the appendices. The version-stamp, pagination, and slight typesetting changes produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
